Weak-instrument-robust confidence sets for proxy-SVAR impulse responses

Source: R/psvar-robust.R
varm_proxy_robust.Rd

Montiel Olea, Stock & Watson (2021) Anderson-Rubin-type confidence sets for the impulse responses to a shock identified with a single external instrument. For each variable \(i\) and horizon \(h\), the set collects all \(\lambda\) for which the (delta-method, HAC) Wald test of \(s\, e_i'\Phi_h\Gamma - \lambda\Gamma_j = 0\) does not reject, where \(\Gamma = E[u_t m_t]\), \(j\) is the target variable and \(s\) is size. The test is a quadratic \(a\lambda^2 + b\lambda + c \le 0\), so the set is one of four types (reported in case):

1

a > 0, discriminant > 0: bounded interval [lower, upper].

2

a < 0, discriminant > 0: the complement of an interval, i.e. (-Inf, r1] U [r2, Inf). lower = -Inf, upper = Inf and the excluded interval (r1, r2) is in gap.

3

a > 0, discriminant < 0: empty set (lower = upper = NA); signals misspecification.

4

otherwise (a < 0, discriminant <= 0): the whole real line (-Inf, Inf); the instrument is uninformative.

0

impact response of target, normalised to size.

Unlike the bootstrap bands of varm_proxy(), these have correct coverage regardless of instrument strength. The covariance of \((\mathrm{vec}(A), \Gamma)\) uses the OLS influence functions with a Bartlett (Newey-West) HAC estimator; derivatives of the MA matrices follow Luetkepohl (2005).

varm_proxy_robust(
  fit,
  m,
  target = 1L,
  size = 1,
  horizon = 20L,
  level = c(0.68, 0.9),
  nwlags = NULL
)

Arguments

fit

a varm() object.

m

proxy: numeric vector (or one-column matrix) of length nrow(fit$Y), aligned with the data (the first p values are dropped to match the residuals).

target

variable (name or position) whose impact response is normalised to size.

size

size of the shock (impact response of target).

horizon

maximum horizon (impact is 0).

level

confidence levels (in (0, 1)).

nwlags

Newey-West truncation lag; default floor(4 * (T/100)^(2/9)).

Value

a varm_proxy_robust object: estimate ((H+1) x K point IRF), lower, upper, case (arrays (H+1) x K x length(level)), gap ((H+1) x K x length(level) x 2, excluded interval in case 2), fstat (see proxy_fstat()), level.

References

Montiel Olea, J. L., Stock, J. H. and Watson, M. W. (2021). Inference in structural vector autoregressions identified with an external instrument. Journal of Econometrics 225(1), 74-87.

Examples

set.seed(1)
e <- matrix(rnorm(600), 300)
y <- matrix(0, 300, 2)
for (t in 2:300) y[t, ] <- 0.5 * y[t - 1, ] + c(e[t, 1] + 0.3 * e[t, 2], e[t, 2] + 0.5 * e[t, 1])
fit <- varm(y, p = 1)
r <- varm_proxy_robust(fit, m = e[, 1] + rnorm(300, sd = 0.5), horizon = 6)
r$lower[, , 2]
#>             y1          y2
#> 0  1.000000000  0.44467847
#> 1  0.347960448  0.10377790
#> 2  0.111524006 -0.01139702
#> 3  0.030156304 -0.03282190
#> 4  0.004596911 -0.02779278
#> 5 -0.001986987 -0.01862251
#> 6 -0.002744429 -0.01125363
